review.title: Removing or selling mortgaged property
review.plain: After mortgaging property, removing it from the county without the mortgagee's written consent, or selling, destroying, or further encumbering it, to defraud the mortgagee, is theft; no punishment is stated here.
acts: takes, drives, carries away, or otherwise removes or permits the taking, driving, or carrying away, or other removal of the mortgaged property
sells, transfers, slaughters, destroys, or in any manner further encumbers the mortgaged property

shared.who: A person who has mortgaged property permitted to be mortgaged by the provisions of Sections 9102 and 9109 of the Commercial Code
intent: With intent to defraud the mortgagee, his or her representative or assigns

penalties.penalty: Guilty of theft, and is punishable accordingly (no punishment is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Takes, drives, carries away, or otherwise removes or permits the taking, driving, or carrying away, or other removal of the mortgaged property, or any part thereof, from the county where it was situated when mortgaged
conditions: During the existence of the mortgage
Without the written consent of the mortgagee
exceptions: Locomotives, engines, rolling stock of a railroad, steamboat machinery in actual use, and vessels are excepted

crimes.act: Sells, transfers, slaughters, destroys, or in any manner further encumbers the mortgaged property, or any part thereof, or causes it to be sold, transferred, slaughtered, destroyed, or further encumbered
ways: causes it to be sold, transferred, slaughtered, destroyed, or further encumbered
conditions: During the existence of the mortgage
exceptions: Locomotives, engines, rolling stock of a railroad, steamboat machinery in actual use, and vessels are excepted

In the case of a sale, transfer, or further encumbrance, at or before the time of making it the mortgagor informs the person to whom it is made of the existence of the prior mortgage, and also informs the prior mortgagee of the intended sale, transfer, or encumbrance, in writing, by giving the name and place of residence of the party to whom it is to be made

review.title: Signing another's name to a newspaper letter
review.plain: Signing someone else's name to a letter and sending it to a newspaper, intending the paper to believe that person wrote it, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: signs any letter addressed to a newspaper with the name of a person other than himself and sends such letter to the newspaper, or causes it to be sent to such newspaper

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Signs any letter addressed to a newspaper with the name of a person other than himself and sends such letter to the newspaper, or causes it to be sent to such newspaper
intent: With intent to lead the newspaper to believe that such letter was written by the person whose name is signed thereto

review.title: Wearing insignia of societies or religious orders
review.plain: Wearing the badge, garb, or insignia of a secret society, fraternal or religious order, or church without being entitled to, or using it to get aid, with intent to deceive, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: wears the badge, lapel button, rosette, or any part of the garb, robe, habit, or any other recognized and established insignia or apparel of any secret society, or fraternal or religious order or organization, or of any sect, church or religious denomination
uses the same to obtain aid or assistance within this State

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Wears the badge, lapel button, rosette, or any part of the garb, robe, habit, or any other recognized and established insignia or apparel of any secret society, or fraternal or religious order or organization, or of any sect, church or religious denomination
exceptions: Entitled to wear and use the same under the constitution, by-laws or rules and regulations, or other laws or enactments of such society, order, organization, sect, church or religious denomination

crimes.act: Uses the same to obtain aid or assistance within this State
exceptions: Entitled to wear and use the same under the constitution, by-laws or rules and regulations, or other laws or enactments of such society, order, organization, sect, church or religious denomination

review.title: Theft of advertising services
review.plain: Attaching or inserting an unauthorized advertisement in a newspaper and redistributing it, or intending to, is the misdemeanor of theft of advertising services; no term is stated here.
acts: attaches or inserts an unauthorized advertisement in a newspaper

penalties.penalty: Guilty of the crime of theft of advertising services which shall be punishable as a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

consequences: A conviction under this section shall not constitute a conviction for petty theft
terms: "Unauthorized advertisement": any form of representation or communication, including any handbill, newsletter, pamphlet, or notice that contains any letters, words, or pictorial representation that is attached to or inserted in a newspaper without a contractual agreement between the publisher and an advertiser
"Newspaper": includes any newspaper, magazine, periodical, or other tangible publication, whether offered for retail sale or distributed without charge

crimes.act: Attaches or inserts an unauthorized advertisement in a newspaper, whether alone or in concert with another
conditions: The person redistributes it to the public or has the intent to redistribute it to the public
exceptions: The publisher or authorized distributor of the newspaper consents to the attachment or insertion of the advertisement
A newspaper distributor who is directed to insert an unauthorized advertisement by a person or company supplying the newspapers, and who is not aware that the advertisement is unauthorized

review.title: Impersonating a peace officer
review.plain: Wearing or using police uniforms, badges, or IDs to fraudulently pose as a law enforcement officer, impersonating one to defraud, or making or selling fake badges is a misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing, of a law enforcement officer
impersonates a law enforcement officer through or on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a law enforcement officer
wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer

makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, insignia, emblem, device, or any label, certificate, card, or writing, which falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer
sells a uniform identifying a law enforcement agency, without verifying that the purchaser is an employee of the agency

terms: "Law enforcement officer" (for subdivisions (a), (b), and (c)): a peace officer as defined in Section 830, and any federal law enforcement officer

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing, of a law enforcement officer
crimes.who: Any person other than one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating a law enforcement officer, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are a law enforcement officer

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Credibly impersonates a law enforcement officer through or on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
crimes.who: Any person other than one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a law enforcement officer
crimes.who: Any person, other than the one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating a law enforcement officer, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are a law enforcement officer

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer, or which so resembles the authorized badge of a law enforcement officer as would deceive any ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer
intent: For the purpose of fraudulently impersonating a law enforcement officer, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are a law enforcement officer

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses, or makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, insignia, emblem, device, or any label, certificate, card, or writing, which falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of a law enforcement officer, or which so resembles the authorized one of a law enforcement officer as would deceive an ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is authorized
exceptions: Identification issued under subdivision (d) by the head of an agency that employs peace officers, stating that the person has honorably retired following service as a peace officer from that agency

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed six months, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine

penalties.if: the person makes or sells any badge under the circumstances described in this subdivision
penalties.penalty: Subject to a fine not to exceed fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000)

consequences: A local law enforcement agency in the jurisdiction that files charges shall seize the badge, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing

crimes.act: Sells a uniform identifying a law enforcement agency, without verifying that the purchaser is an employee of the agency
exceptions: The uniform is to be used solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, video production, or a theatrical event, and prior written permission has been obtained from the identified law enforcement agency

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000)

review.title: Impersonating a firefighter
review.plain: Wearing or using fire department uniforms, badges, or IDs to fraudulently pose as a firefighter or fire marshal, making or selling fake badges, or falsely claiming fire authority to sell equipment is a misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of an officer or member of a fire department or a deputy state fire marshal
impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a fire department or the Office of the State Fire Marshal
wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal

makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, insignia, emblem, device, or any label, certificate, card, or writing, which falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer, or member of a fire department or a deputy state fire marshal
falsely represents, in any manner whatsoever, to any other person that they are a fire marshal, fire inspector or member of a fire department
sells a uniform identifying a firefighting agency or department without verifying that the purchaser is an employee or authorized member of the agency or department

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of an officer or member of a fire department or a deputy state fire marshal
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code representing firefighters or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
crimes.who: Any person, other than an officer or member of a fire department
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating an officer or member of a fire department or the Office of the State Fire Marshal, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an officer or member of a fire department or the Office of the State Fire Marshal

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Credibly impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code representing firefighters or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
crimes.who: Any person, other than an officer or member of a fire department

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a fire department or the Office of the State Fire Marshal
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code representing firefighters or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
crimes.who: Any person, other than the one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating an officer, or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal, or which so resembles the authorized badge as would deceive any ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is authorized
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code representing firefighters or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
intent: For the purpose of fraudulently impersonating an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an officer or member of a fire department, or a deputy state fire marshal

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses, or makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, insignia, emblem, device, or any label, certificate, card, or writing, which falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer, or member of a fire department or a deputy state fire marshal, or which so resembles the authorized one as would deceive an ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is authorized
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code representing firefighters or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

penalties.if: the person makes or sells any badge under the circumstances described in this subdivision
penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000)

crimes.act: Falsely represents, in any manner whatsoever, to any other person that they are a fire marshal, fire inspector or member of a fire department, or that they have the approval, endorsement or authorization of any fire marshal, fire inspector or fire department, or member thereof
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code representing firefighters or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
intent: For the purpose of selling, leasing or otherwise disposing of merchandise, supplies or equipment used in fire prevention or suppression

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Sells a uniform identifying a firefighting agency or department without verifying that the purchaser is an employee or authorized member of the agency or department
exceptions: The uniform is to be used solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, video production, or a theatrical event, and prior written permission has been obtained from the identified firefighting agency or department

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars ($1,000)

review.title: Impersonating a utility employee
review.plain: Presenting oneself to a utility customer to fraudulently pose as a public utility or district employee, or credibly impersonating one to defraud, is a misdemeanor punishable by up to six months in county jail.
acts: presents themselves to a utility or district customer
impersonates an employee of a public utility or district on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means

shared.who: Any person, other than an employee of a public utility or district as defined in Sections 216 and 11503 of the Public Utilities Code, respectively

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed six months, or by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000), or by both that fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Presents themselves to a utility or district customer
exceptions: Conduct that arguably constitutes protected activity under state labor law or the National Labor Relations Act (Title 29, United States Code, Section 151 and following)
intent: With the intent of fraudulently personating an employee of a public utility or district, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an employee of a public utility or district

crimes.act: Credibly impersonates an employee of a public utility or district on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
exceptions: Conduct that arguably constitutes protected activity under state labor law or the National Labor Relations Act (Title 29, United States Code, Section 151 and following)

review.title: Impersonating a government officer or employee
review.plain: Wearing or using a public officer's or employee's badge, ID card, or insignia to fraudulently pose as one, impersonating one to defraud, or making or selling fake badges is a misdemeanor; no jail term is stated here.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized badge, photographic identification card, or insignia of a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee
impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means

makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, photographic identification card, or insignia, which falsely purports to be for the use of a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized badge, photographic identification card, or insignia of a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
crimes.who: Any person, other than a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee
intent: With the intent of fraudulently personating a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Credibly impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated
crimes.who: Any person, other than a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses, or makes, sells, loans, gives, or transfers to another, any badge, photographic identification card, or insignia, which falsely purports to be for the use of a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee, or which so resembles the authorized one as would deceive an ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is authorized for use by a state, county, city, special district, or city and county officer or employee
exceptions: Use of a badge solely as a prop for a motion picture, television, or video production, or an entertainment or theatrical event
A badge supplied by a recognized employee organization as defined in Section 3501 of the Government Code or a state or international organization to which it is affiliated

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

penalties.if: the person makes or sells any badge under the circumstances described in this subdivision
penalties.penalty: Subject to a fine not to exceed fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000)

review.title: Impersonating search and rescue personnel
review.plain: Wearing or using search and rescue uniforms or badges to fraudulently pose as a team member or obtain aid or money, or impersonating one to defraud, is a misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail for badge misuse.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team
uses the same to obtain aid, money, or assistance within this state
impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

terms: "Member": any natural person who is registered with an accredited disaster council for the purpose of engaging in disaster service without pay or other consideration; food and lodging provided, or expenses reimbursed for these items, during a member's activation do not constitute other consideration

"Search and rescue unit or team": an entity engaged in the acts of searching for, rescuing, or recovering by means of ground, marine, or air activity, any person that becomes lost, injured, or is killed while outdoors or as a result of a natural or manmade disaster, including instances involving searches for downed or missing aircraft

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the authorized uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team
crimes.who: Any person, other than an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Uses the same to obtain aid, money, or assistance within this state
crimes.who: Any person, other than an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Credibly impersonates such an officer or member on an internet website, by other electronic means, or by any other means
crimes.who: Any person, other than an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the badge of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team
crimes.who: Any person, other than the one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team, or fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine

crimes.act: Wears or uses any badge that falsely purports to be authorized for the use of one who by law is given the authority of an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team, or that resembles the authorized badge as would deceive any ordinary reasonable person into believing that it is authorized
intent: For the purpose of fraudulently impersonating an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team, or of fraudulently inducing the belief that they are an officer or member of a government agency managed or affiliated search and rescue unit or team

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that fine and imprisonment

review.title: Impersonating a first responder during evacuations
review.plain: Fraudulently posing as a first responder in an area under an evacuation order, or impersonating one online during or within 30 days after an evacuation order to defraud, is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term.
acts: wears, exhibits, or uses the uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of a first responder
impersonates a first responder on an internet website, or by other electronic means

shared.who: Any person, other than a first responder

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, by a fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or by both that imprisonment and fine, or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 and by a fine not to exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000)

terms: "Evacuation order": has the same meaning as in Section 463

"First responder": a first responder as defined under Section 8562 of the Government Code, or any employee of the Federal Emergency Management Agency under Section 313 of Subchapter V of Chapter 1 of Title 6 of the United States Code

crimes.act: Wears, exhibits, or uses the uniform, insignia, emblem, device, label, certificate, card, or writing of a first responder
intent: With the intent of fraudulently impersonating a first responder in an area subject to an evacuation order

crimes.act: Credibly impersonates a first responder on an internet website, or by other electronic means
conditions: During an evacuation order or within 30 days of its termination

review.title: Wire fraud to obtain public utility information
review.plain: Transmitting communications by wire, radio, or television to obtain a public utility's confidential information, trade secrets, or customer records by false pretenses is punishable by up to one year in county jail or a felony jail term.
acts: transmits or causes to be transmitted by means of wire, radio or television communication any words, sounds, writings, signs, signals, or pictures

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170, or by imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year

crimes.act: Transmits or causes to be transmitted by means of wire, radio or television communication any words, sounds, writings, signs, signals, or pictures
intent: For the purpose of furthering or executing a scheme or artifice to obtain, from a public utility, confidential, privileged, or proprietary information, trade secrets, trade lists, customer records, billing records, customer credit data, or accounting data by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, personations, or promises

review.title: False certification of community service
review.plain: Certifying, with intent to defraud, that someone ordered to do community service as a probation condition finished the required hours when they did not is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: certifies that a person ordered by the court to participate in community service as a condition of probation has completed the number of hours of community service prescribed in the court order

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Certifies that a person ordered by the court to participate in community service as a condition of probation has completed the number of hours of community service prescribed in the court order
conditions: The participant has not completed the prescribed number of hours

review.title: Destroying insured property to defraud insurer
review.plain: Willfully injuring, destroying, hiding, abandoning, or disposing of insured property to defraud the insurer is a felony punishable by two, three, or five years and a fine up to $50,000, plus two years per prior conviction.
acts: injures, destroys, secretes, abandons, or disposes of any property which at the time is insured against loss or damage by theft, or embezzlement, or any casualty

crimes.act: Injures, destroys, secretes, abandons, or disposes of any property which at the time is insured against loss or damage by theft, or embezzlement, or any casualty, whether the property is the property or in the possession of that person or any other person
intent: With intent to defraud or prejudice the insurer

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for two, three, or five years and by a fine not exceeding fifty thousand dollars ($50,000)

penalties.if: the person has a prior conviction of the offense set forth in subdivision (a), in Section 550, or in former Section 556 or former Section 1871.1 of the Insurance Code
penalties.penalty: A two-year enhancement for each prior conviction in addition to the sentence provided under subdivision (a)

review.title: Referring business for insurance fraud
review.plain: Soliciting, accepting, or referring business knowing or recklessly disregarding that someone intends to commit insurance fraud is punishable by up to one year in county jail or up to three years, a large fine, and restitution.
acts: solicits, accepts, or refers any business to or from any individual or entity

crimes.act: Solicits, accepts, or refers any business to or from any individual or entity
knowledge: With the knowledge that the individual or entity for or from whom the solicitation or referral is made, or the individual or entity who is solicited or referred, intends to violate Section 550 of this code or Section 1871.4 of the Insurance Code
mentalState: With reckless disregard for whether the individual or entity intends to violate Section 550 of this code or Section 1871.4 of the Insurance Code

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for 16 months, two years, or three years, or by a fine not exceeding fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) or double the amount of the fraud, whichever is greater, or by both that imprisonment and fine

penalties.if: a second or subsequent conviction
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 or by that imprisonment and a fine of fifty thousand dollars ($50,000)

consequences: Restitution shall be ordered, including restitution for any medical evaluation or treatment services obtained or provided

review.title: Insurance fraud
review.plain: Knowingly presenting false insurance or health care claims, staging vehicle collisions, or making false statements to support or oppose insurance claims is punishable by up to five years plus enhancements, fines, and restitution.
acts: present or cause to be presented any false or fraudulent claim for the payment of a loss or injury
present multiple claims for the same loss or injury
cause or participate in a vehicular collision, or any other vehicular accident
present a false or fraudulent claim for the payments of a loss for theft, destruction, damage, or conversion of a motor vehicle
prepare, make, or subscribe any writing
make or cause to be made any false or fraudulent claim for payment of a health care benefit
submit a claim for a health care benefit that was not used by, or on behalf of, the claimant
present multiple claims for payment of the same health care benefit
present for payment any undercharges for health care benefits on behalf of a specific claimant
Present or cause to be presented any written or oral statement as part of, or in support of or opposition to, a claim for payment or other benefit pursuant to an insurance policy
Prepare or make any written or oral statement that is intended to be presented to any insurer or any insurance claimant
Conceal
fail to disclose the occurrence of, an event that affects any person
Prepare or make any written or oral statement, intended to be presented to any insurer or producer for the purpose of obtaining a motor vehicle insurance policy

consequences: Restitution shall be ordered, including restitution for any medical evaluation or treatment services obtained or provided

review.title: Posted-property article exceptions for officers and roads
review.plain: Says the posted-property trespass article does not apply to entries by peace officers or other authorized public officers on duty, or to lawful use of an existing public road right of way.

review.title: Posted-property article exceptions for labor activity
review.plain: Says the posted-property trespass article does not prohibit lawful labor union organizing activity or authorized union investigations of working-condition safety on posted property.

review.title: Posted-property definitions
review.plain: Defines "sign," "posted property," and "posted boundary" for the posted-property trespass article.

review.title: Property that may be posted against trespassing
review.plain: Lists the kinds of utility, oil, gas, water, explosives, railroad, sewer, and quarry property that may be posted against trespassing and loitering.

review.title: How property is posted against trespassing
review.plain: Sets where and how often signs must be placed to post property described in Section 554 against trespassing and loitering, depending on fencing, size, and type of structure.

review.title: Entering posted property
review.plain: Entering or remaining on posted property without the written permission of the owner, tenant, or occupant is unlawful, and each day is a separate offense; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: enter or remain upon any posted property

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

consequences: Guilty of a separate offense for each day during any portion of which he enters or remains upon such posted property

crimes.act: Enters or remains upon any posted property
conditions: Without the written permission of the owner, tenant, or occupant in legal possession or control thereof

review.title: Destroying posted-property signs
review.plain: Tearing down, defacing, or destroying a sign posted under the posted-property article without authority is unlawful; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: tear down, deface or destroy any sign posted pursuant to this article

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

crimes.act: Tears down, defaces or destroys any sign posted pursuant to this article

review.title: Loitering near posted property
review.plain: Loitering in the immediate vicinity of posted property is unlawful, though picketing and lawful labor-dispute publicity are allowed; no punishment is stated in this section.
acts: loiter in the immediate vicinity of any posted property

penalties.penalty: No punishment is stated in this section

crimes.act: Loiters in the immediate vicinity of any posted property
exceptions: Picketing in such immediate vicinity or any lawful activity by which the public is informed of the existence of an alleged labor dispute

review.title: Posted-property violations are misdemeanors
review.plain: Violating any provision of the posted-property trespass article is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: Violation of any of the provisions of this article

penalties.penalty: Misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Violation of any of the provisions of this article

review.title: Posted-property article applies statewide
review.plain: Makes the posted-property article apply in all counties and cities and bars local ordinances that conflict with it.

review.title: Posted-property article severability
review.plain: Provides that if any part of the posted-property article is held invalid, the rest remains in effect.

review.title: Advertising signs on public property
review.plain: Placing or keeping advertising signs, pictures, or devices on state, city, or county property without lawful permission is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: place or maintain, or cause to be placed or maintained

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Places or maintains, or causes to be placed or maintained upon any property of the State, or of a city or of a county, any sign, picture, transparency, advertisement, or mechanical device which is used for the purpose of advertising or which advertises or brings to notice any person, article of merchandise, business or profession, or anything that is to be or has been sold, bartered, or given away

review.title: Advertising signs on private property
review.plain: Placing or keeping advertising signs, pictures, or devices on property where one has no estate or right of possession, without the owner's or possessor's prior consent, is a misdemeanor; no term is stated here.
acts: place or maintain or cause to be placed or maintained upon any property in which he has no estate or right of possession

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a misdemeanor (no term is stated in this section)

crimes.act: Places or maintains or causes to be placed or maintained upon any property in which he has no estate or right of possession any sign, picture, transparency, advertisement, or mechanical device which is used for the purpose of advertising, or which advertises or brings to notice any person, article of merchandise, business or profession, or anything that is to be or has been sold, bartered, or given away
conditions: Without the consent of the owner, lessee, or person in lawful possession of such property before the sign, picture, transparency, advertisement, or mechanical device is placed upon the property

review.title: Exceptions to sign-posting crimes
review.plain: Says Sections 556 and 556.1 do not bar legally required or court-ordered notices, notices about the premises where posted, or public highway and street name, direction, or condition signs.
